title: ConvFrontend class copy-pasted across 5 files (4 archived + 1 live)
description: An identical ConvFrontend nn.Module (conv1 2->32 k5, pool, LIF beta=0.9; conv2 32->64 k5, pool, LIF; flatten; sum over time) is duplicated verbatim in five places, including the LIVE code/final_evaluation.py. Five divergent copies of the visual backbone frontend are a maintenance hazard: a numerics fix to one (e.g. reset semantics, beta) will silently not propagate to the others.
evidence: verify_full.py:26-46; verify_simulators.py:27-47; verify_brian2_raw.py:30-50; debug_brian2_exact.py:19-39; code/final_evaluation.py:33-53 (LIVE). All byte-identical bodies.

Verify the extraction is numerically inert (same beta, same reset_hidden order) before touching the live final_evaluation.py.

title: Sim-vs-sim agreement is NOT SpiNNaker-hardware verification; no energy/latency producible
description: The cluster checks that a PyTorch discrete-time simulator matches Brian2/PyNN IF_curr_exp and prints verdicts like 'VERIFIED: PyTorch discrete-time simulator matches Brian2/PyNN'. Brian2 is a SOFTWARE simulator; comments assert the equations are 'exact same as PyNN/SpiNNaker' (verify_brian2_raw.py:180; docstring line 6). Per project rules (mapping != inference != real hardware; nothing has run on a board), treating a 'VERIFIED' stdout line as evidence of on-chip correctness would be an overclaim. No energy or latency figure is or can be produced by these scripts — a simulator cannot yield real hardware energy. No hardcoded result numbers were found in the cluster itself (all counts/matches are computed).
evidence: verify_brian2_raw.py:180 comment 'exact same as PyNN/SpiNNaker'; verify_full.py:343 'VERIFIED ... matches Brian2/PyNN'; verify_simulators.py:348 same; no energy/accuracy literals presented as results in the cluster.
fix: Documentation-level: if any of this is cited, label it 'PyTorch-vs-Brian2 software-simulator numerical agreement', never 'SpiNNaker-verified'. Do not derive energy/latency from it. Keep the hardware claims in HARDWARE_ACCESS_CHECKLIST/SpiNNaker plan as unchecked hypotheses.

title: Hardcoded baseline numbers printed in a BASELINE COMPARISON table (RULE 1)
description: main() prints a 'BASELINE COMPARISON' table whose baseline rows are hardcoded literals — A_no_align '~97.0% / ~13.3%', Frozen-C '13.3% / 14.8%', Unfrozen+rehearsal '95.7% / 14.4%' — interleaved with the run's own computed mean_retention/mean_v2a on the final row. Under RULE 1, hardcoded numbers presented next to measured ones as a results table is exactly the pattern that poisons trust; the '~' values read as estimates. These go to stdout only (not paper/CSV), and the file is archived, which bounds the harm.
evidence: literals hardcoded in code at lines 758-761 ('~97.0%','~13.3%','13.3%','14.8%','95.7%','14.4%'); computed values mean_v2a/mean_retention lines 755-756.
fix: If this experiment is ever revived (in v2), source every baseline number from its CSV or drop the row; never print hardcoded comparison numbers beside measured ones. For retirement, this is one more reason to DELETE v1 (ARCH-001).

title: Held-out-class masking is a no-op: held-out digits are still trained on
description: train_correspondence uses ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss() with default reduction='mean', so loss_vis/loss_aud/loss are SCALARS (lines 412-414). The held-out masking then does loss = loss * mask.float() (scalar broadcast to a per-sample vector) then loss.sum()/mask.sum() (lines 418-419), which algebraically returns the original scalar mean over ALL samples — the held-out classes were never excluded. Compounding this, build_paired_feature_dataset accepts held_out_classes (line 299) but never uses it, so held-out samples are also present in the training set. Net effect: the step-7 'held-out-class' test (digits 8,9, lines 616-628) evaluates alignment on classes the model was actually trained on, invalidating that result and the derived 'discovered vs engineered' verdict (line 651).
evidence: nn.CrossEntropyLoss() default mean at line 377; scalar loss lines 412-414; scalar*mask then sum/sum lines 418-419; held_out_classes param unused in build_paired_feature_dataset (declared line 299); held-out run at lines 622-628.
fix: To actually hold classes out: use reduction='none' to get per-sample losses BEFORE masking, or filter held-out samples out of the dataset in build_paired_feature_dataset. As-is the held-out numbers are meaningless. For retirement this is a primary reason v1 was superseded (ARCH-001) — confirm v2 fixed it.

title: Dead vis_indices/aud_indices loop that still consumes the RNG
description: In build_paired_feature_dataset the first per-class loop builds vis_indices/aud_indices via rng.choice (lines 313-322) and they are never read — a follow-up comment 'Actually we need PAIRED samples' recomputes everything in a second loop (lines 326-343). The dead loop is not inert: it advances the same rng (created line 312), so the real paired selection at lines 335-336 draws different samples than it would without the dead loop. Removing it would change which samples train the projection heads, i.e. it is dead code with a numeric side effect.
evidence: unused vis_indices/aud_indices lines 313-322 vs paired recompute lines 326-343; shared rng line 312 consumed by both.
fix: Delete the dead loop, but note it will change results (RNG stream shifts); acceptable only because the file is being retired. If preserving v1 outputs bit-for-bit, leave it. Prefer DELETE the whole file (ARCH-001).

title: Null baseline shuffles only 2 held-out classes -> 50% chance it equals same-class
description: compute_held_out_alignment builds its null baseline by np.random.shuffle of the held-out class list (line 526), but held_out_classes=(8,9) has just two elements, so the shuffle is the identity with probability 0.5. When identity, null_sims compares each class prototype with itself, making null_baseline equal to same-class similarity and the verdict test (same_class > null_baseline + 0.1, line 651) meaningless. Uses the global numpy RNG (seeded line 550), not the local rng. Compounds ARCH-015.
evidence: np.random.shuffle(shuffled_classes) line 526 with held_out_classes length 2; verdict comparison line 651.
fix: Use a permutation that excludes fixed points, or average many derangements, or use off_diag as the control; and use a local Generator. Retirement: another reason v1 held-out numbers are untrustworthy.

title: forgetting_T1_T3 stores the incremental T2->T3 drop, not total T1->T3 forgetting
description: forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3 (line 412, self-labeled 'incremental T2->T3'). Its name implies total forgetting of T1 through T3, but total T1 forgetting is total_forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t3 (line 414). A downstream reader/aggregator that treats the column named forgetting_T1_T3 as total forgetting will understate/mislabel the headline forgetting metric — sensitive given RULE 5 (the forgetting claim must be reported honestly).
evidence: forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3 line 412; total_forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t3 line 414; both written to CSV lines 437,439 and re-read by aggregate_confirmation_results metrics list lines 486-487.
fix: Rename the column to forgetting_T1_incremental_T2_T3 (or similar) so the incremental vs total distinction is unambiguous in the CSV consumed downstream. Retirement: note the ambiguity for anyone mining old cl_confirmation CSVs.

title: forgetting_T2_T3 and total_forgetting_T2_T3 are identical duplicate columns
description: forgetting_T2_T3 = acc_t2_after - acc_t2_after_t3 (line 413) and total_forgetting_T2_T3 = acc_t2_after - acc_t2_after_t3 (line 415) are computed from the same two quantities and are therefore always equal. Both are written to the CSV and both appear in the aggregation metrics list, producing two identically-valued summary rows and inviting double-counting.
evidence: identical RHS at lines 413 and 415; both in EXPECTED_COLUMNS (lines 76-77) and metrics list (lines 486-487).
fix: Drop one of the two columns (keep total_forgetting_T2_T3 for consistency with T1) in any revived version. Retirement: flag so old summaries are read knowing the two columns are redundant.

title: 95% CI uses normal z=1.96 with n=2-3 seeds
description: aggregate_confirmation_results computes ci95 = 1.96 * std / sqrt(n) (line 497) and writes ci95_lower/ci95_upper labeled as 95% CI. With the seed policy [42,123,456] n is 2-3, where the normal approximation is inappropriate — a t-multiplier (e.g. t_.975,df=2 ~ 4.30) would be far wider. Labeling a z-based interval '95% CI' at n<=3 overstates precision.
evidence: ci95 = 1.96 * std / np.sqrt(n) line 497; std uses ddof=1 line 495; seeds=[42,123,456] line 539.
fix: Use scipy.stats.t.ppf for small-n intervals, or report mean +/- std with explicit n rather than a CI, and label accordingly. Retirement: any 'CI' from this script should be treated as under-wide.
